diuretics.moa: Loop diuretics (furosemide, bumetanide, torsemide) block Na-K-2Cl cotransport in the thick ascending limb; thiazides (hydrochlorothiazide, chlorthalidone, indapamide) block Na-Cl in the distal tubule; potassium-sparing drugs block ENaC (amiloride, triamterene) or aldosterone receptors (spironolactone, eplerenone); carbonic anhydrase inhibitors (acetazolamide) reduce bicarbonate reabsorption; osmotic diuretics (mannitol) hold water in the tubule
diuretics.uses: Oedema of heart, liver and kidney disease; hypertension; acute pulmonary oedema; ascites; hypercalcaemia (loop); nephrogenic diabetes insipidus (thiazide); cerebral oedema and raised ICP (mannitol); glaucoma and altitude sickness (acetazolamide); hyperaldosteronism
diuretics.adr: Loop and thiazide: hypokalaemia, hyponatraemia, hypovolaemia, metabolic alkalosis, hyperuricaemia and hyperglycaemia; loop: ototoxicity; potassium-sparing: hyperkalaemia; spironolactone: gynaecomastia; acetazolamide: acidosis and paraesthesia; mannitol: fluid overload
diuretics.ci: Anuria, severe hypovolaemia, hypokalaemia (loop and thiazide), hyperkalaemia and renal failure (potassium-sparing), gout, sulfonamide allergy; mannitol in heart failure and active intracranial bleeding; take care with digoxin and lithium

antidiuretics.moa: ADH (vasopressin) and desmopressin act on V2 receptors to insert aquaporin-2 water channels in the collecting duct; thiazides lower urine volume in nephrogenic diabetes insipidus; chlorpropamide and carbamazepine enhance or mimic ADH
antidiuretics.uses: Central diabetes insipidus, nocturnal enuresis, haemophilia A and von Willebrand disease (desmopressin raises factor VIII), bleeding oesophageal varices (terlipressin, vasopressin)
antidiuretics.adr: Water intoxication, hyponatraemia, headache and nausea; vasopressin: hypertension, abdominal cramps and coronary and peripheral vasoconstriction
antidiuretics.ci: Desmopressin: hyponatraemia, heart failure and habitual polydipsia; vasopressin: coronary artery disease, hypertension, asthma and chronic nephritis

haematinics.moa: Iron is needed for haemoglobin synthesis; vitamin B12 and folic acid are needed for DNA synthesis in maturing red cells; vitamin C, copper, pyridoxine and riboflavin assist; erythropoietin stimulates red cell production in the marrow
haematinics.uses: Iron-deficiency anaemia (oral iron first, parenteral if not tolerated or not absorbed); pernicious anaemia (B12); megaloblastic anaemia (folic acid); anaemia of chronic kidney disease (erythropoietin)
haematinics.adr: Oral iron: nausea, epigastric pain, constipation or diarrhoea, black stools and staining of teeth by liquids; injectable iron: anaphylaxis, pain and staining at the injection site; erythropoietin: hypertension, thrombosis and pure red cell aplasia
haematinics.ci: Iron in haemochromatosis, haemosiderosis, haemolytic anaemia and repeated transfusion; iron overdose is dangerous in children (treat with desferrioxamine); folic acid alone in B12 deficiency (worsens neuropathy); erythropoietin in uncontrolled hypertension

coagulants.moa: Vitamin K is a cofactor for γ-carboxylation of clotting factors II, VII, IX and X; others replace factors (fibrinogen, antihaemophilic factor), release factor VIII (desmopressin) or reduce capillary bleeding (ethamsylate, adrenochrome)
coagulants.uses: Vitamin K deficiency bleeding in newborns, obstructive jaundice and warfarin overdose; haemophilia (factor VIII); local bleeding; menorrhagia
coagulants.adr: Vitamin K: rare anaphylaxis with IV injection; haemolysis in G6PD deficiency and in newborns (menadione); thrombosis with factor concentrates
coagulants.ci: Menadione in G6PD deficiency and neonates; give vitamin K IV slowly; avoid in thromboembolic disease where possible

anticoagulants.moa: Heparin (UFH and LMWH) activates antithrombin III, inactivating thrombin and factor Xa; fondaparinux, rivaroxaban and apixaban inhibit factor Xa; dabigatran, argatroban and bivalirudin inhibit thrombin directly; warfarin blocks vitamin K epoxide reductase, lowering factors II, VII, IX and X; citrate and EDTA chelate calcium in vitro
anticoagulants.uses: Venous thromboembolism and pulmonary embolism, stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation, acute coronary syndromes, prosthetic heart valves, dialysis circuits and blood storage
anticoagulants.adr: Bleeding (the main risk); heparin-induced thrombocytopenia; osteoporosis with long-term heparin; warfarin: skin necrosis, teratogenicity and many drug interactions; dabigatran: dyspepsia
anticoagulants.ci: Active bleeding, bleeding disorders, severe hypertension, recent surgery or haemorrhagic stroke, peptic ulcer; warfarin in pregnancy; LMWH in severe renal impairment; antidotes: protamine (heparin), vitamin K and prothrombin complex (warfarin), idarucizumab (dabigatran), andexanet (Xa inhibitors)

fibrinolytics.moa: Streptokinase, urokinase, alteplase, reteplase and tenecteplase convert plasminogen to plasmin, which breaks down fibrin clots
fibrinolytics.uses: Acute myocardial infarction, ischaemic stroke within the time window, massive pulmonary embolism, deep vein thrombosis, blocked catheters and shunts
fibrinolytics.adr: Bleeding (including intracranial), hypotension and reperfusion arrhythmias; streptokinase: allergy, fever and antibodies after earlier exposure
fibrinolytics.ci: Active bleeding, recent surgery or trauma, haemorrhagic stroke, intracranial tumour, severe uncontrolled hypertension, aortic dissection, pregnancy; repeat streptokinase within 6 months or after a streptococcal infection

antifibrinolytics.moa: Tranexamic acid and aminocaproic acid block the lysine-binding sites of plasminogen, so it cannot attach to fibrin; aprotinin inhibits plasmin directly
antifibrinolytics.uses: Heavy menstrual bleeding, bleeding after trauma and surgery, postpartum haemorrhage, dental extraction in haemophilia, reversal of fibrinolytic therapy
antifibrinolytics.adr: Nausea, diarrhoea, dizziness, thrombosis, seizures at high doses, ureteric clots in haematuria; aprotinin: anaphylaxis
antifibrinolytics.ci: Active thromboembolic disease, haematuria from the upper urinary tract (clot colic), disseminated intravascular coagulation; reduce the dose in renal impairment

antiplatelet-drugs.moa: Aspirin irreversibly inhibits COX-1 and stops thromboxane A2; clopidogrel, prasugrel and ticagrelor block the P2Y12 ADP receptor; dipyridamole and cilostazol raise cAMP; abciximab, eptifibatide and tirofiban block glycoprotein IIb/IIIa receptors
antiplatelet-drugs.uses: Prevention after MI and stroke, acute coronary syndromes, coronary stents, peripheral arterial disease, cardiac surgery and graft thrombosis
antiplatelet-drugs.adr: Bleeding; gastric irritation (aspirin); thrombocytopenia (GP IIb/IIIa blockers); clopidogrel: neutropenia and TTP (rare); dipyridamole: headache and dizziness; ticagrelor: dyspnoea
antiplatelet-drugs.ci: Active bleeding, peptic ulcer, bleeding disorders and recent haemorrhagic stroke; stop clopidogrel 5 to 7 days before surgery; aspirin in children with viral infection; avoid combining with anticoagulants unless needed

hypolipidaemic-drugs.moa: Statins inhibit HMG-CoA reductase, lowering liver cholesterol synthesis and raising LDL receptors; fibrates activate PPARα and lower triglycerides; bile acid sequestrants (cholestyramine) bind bile acids; ezetimibe blocks cholesterol absorption; niacin lowers VLDL and LDL release; PCSK9 inhibitors (evolocumab) increase LDL receptors; omega-3 fatty acids reduce triglycerides
hypolipidaemic-drugs.uses: Hypercholesterolaemia and prevention of heart attack and stroke (statins); hypertriglyceridaemia (fibrates, omega-3, niacin); statin-intolerant patients (ezetimibe, resins); familial hypercholesterolaemia (PCSK9 inhibitors)
hypolipidaemic-drugs.adr: Statins: myalgia, myopathy, rhabdomyolysis and raised liver enzymes; fibrates: myopathy and gallstones; resins: constipation, bloating and reduced absorption of other drugs; niacin: flushing, itching, hyperglycaemia and gout
hypolipidaemic-drugs.ci: Statins: pregnancy, breastfeeding and active liver disease; fibrates: severe renal or liver disease, gallbladder disease and with statins (myopathy risk); resins: complete biliary obstruction and hypertriglyceridaemia

plasma-expanders.moa: Large molecules (dextran, gelatin, hydroxyethyl starch, albumin) stay in the blood vessels and draw fluid in by oncotic pressure, increasing plasma volume
plasma-expanders.uses: Hypovolaemic shock from haemorrhage, burns or severe dehydration when blood is not available; albumin in hypoalbuminaemia and after paracentesis
plasma-expanders.adr: Anaphylactoid reactions, circulatory overload and pulmonary oedema, bleeding from interference with clotting (dextran, starch), renal injury (starch), interference with cross-matching (dextran)
plasma-expanders.ci: Heart failure, severe renal failure, bleeding disorders and hypersensitivity; hydroxyethyl starch in sepsis and critical illness

drugs-for-peptic-ulcer.moa: PPIs (omeprazole, pantoprazole, rabeprazole) irreversibly block the H+-K+ ATPase; H2 blockers (ranitidine, famotidine) block histamine H2 receptors; antacids neutralise acid; sucralfate and bismuth coat the ulcer; misoprostol replaces prostaglandins; antibiotics (clarithromycin, amoxicillin, metronidazole) eradicate H. pylori
drugs-for-peptic-ulcer.uses: Peptic ulcer, GERD, H. pylori eradication (PPI plus two antibiotics), Zollinger-Ellison syndrome, NSAID ulcer prevention and stress ulcer prophylaxis
drugs-for-peptic-ulcer.adr: PPIs: headache, diarrhoea, low magnesium and B12, fractures and Clostridium difficile with long use; H2 blockers: dizziness, and cimetidine: gynaecomastia and enzyme inhibition; antacids: constipation (aluminium), diarrhoea (magnesium) and milk-alkali syndrome; sucralfate: constipation; bismuth: black stools
drugs-for-peptic-ulcer.ci: Antacids containing magnesium or aluminium in renal failure; misoprostol in pregnancy; sucralfate in renal failure; clarithromycin interactions; PPIs may mask gastric cancer, so investigate alarm features

antiemetics.moa: Anticholinergics (hyoscine) and H1 blockers (promethazine, dimenhydrinate) act on the vestibular system and vomiting centre; D2 blockers (metoclopramide, domperidone, prochlorperazine, haloperidol) act on the chemoreceptor trigger zone; 5-HT3 blockers (ondansetron, granisetron) block gut and CTZ receptors; NK1 blockers (aprepitant); corticosteroids; cannabinoids; benzodiazepines
antiemetics.uses: Motion sickness, vertigo, chemotherapy and radiotherapy vomiting, postoperative nausea, nausea of pregnancy (doxylamine and pyridoxine), gastroparesis (prokinetics) and migraine
antiemetics.adr: Metoclopramide: extrapyramidal reactions (dystonia in children and young women), drowsiness and hyperprolactinaemia; domperidone: QT prolongation; ondansetron: headache, constipation and QT prolongation; H1 blockers and anticholinergics: sedation and dry mouth
antiemetics.ci: Metoclopramide: intestinal obstruction, GI bleeding, Parkinson's disease and caution in children; domperidone: cardiac disease and long QT; ondansetron: congenital long QT; anticholinergics: glaucoma and prostatic hypertrophy

laxatives.moa: Bulk-forming agents (ispaghula, bran) swell and stimulate peristalsis; stool softeners (docusate, liquid paraffin) lubricate or wet the stool; osmotic agents (lactulose, magnesium sulphate, polyethylene glycol) hold water in the gut; stimulants (bisacodyl, senna, castor oil) increase peristalsis and secretion
laxatives.uses: Constipation, bowel preparation before surgery or colonoscopy, hepatic encephalopathy (lactulose), avoiding straining after surgery or in haemorrhoids, and removing toxins in poisoning
laxatives.adr: Bloating, cramps and flatulence; diarrhoea with dehydration and low potassium; dependence and atonic colon with stimulant misuse; liquid paraffin: lipoid pneumonia and malabsorption of vitamins A, D, E and K; magnesium salts: hypermagnesaemia in renal failure
laxatives.ci: Intestinal obstruction, undiagnosed abdominal pain, acute abdomen, inflammatory bowel disease (stimulants), pregnancy (castor oil), renal failure (magnesium and phosphate preparations) and children (stimulants without advice)

drugs-for-diarrhoea.moa: Oral rehydration solution uses glucose-sodium co-transport to replace fluid; antimicrobials treat infective causes; probiotics restore gut flora; loperamide and diphenoxylate stimulate gut opioid receptors to slow motility; racecadotril blocks enkephalinase; bismuth and kaolin adsorb; aminosalicylates (sulfasalazine, mesalamine), steroids and immunosuppressants treat inflammatory bowel disease
drugs-for-diarrhoea.uses: Acute watery diarrhoea (ORS and zinc first), traveller's diarrhoea, cholera, amoebic and bacillary dysentery, ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease
drugs-for-diarrhoea.adr: Loperamide: constipation, abdominal distension and toxic megacolon; diphenoxylate: sedation and anticholinergic effects; sulfasalazine: rash, nausea, oligospermia and blood disorders; steroid effects
drugs-for-diarrhoea.ci: Antimotility drugs in dysentery, bloody diarrhoea, high fever, pseudomembranous colitis, toxic megacolon and in young children; sulfasalazine in sulfonamide or salicylate allergy
